To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the net energy for lactation in calcium salts of fatty acids from palm oils is 6.52 +/- 1.74 Mcal/kg dry matter.
the NEL of calcium salt of long chain fatty acids from palm fatty acids was 6.52 (1.74) Mcal/kg DM and the efficiency of the use was 77.4% for lactating cows.
calcium salts of long chain fatty acids from palm kernel oil are a valuable source of energy for lactating dairy cows fed silage based diets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of calcium salts of fatty acids as a fat supplement in diets of dairy cows.
the use of calcium salts of fatty acids as an energy source for lactating cows.

the effect of feeding calcium salts of long chain fatty acids on the net energy for lactation and the efficiency of use of metabolizable protein for lactation in cows fed diets with varying amounts of protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NEL of calcium salt of long-chain fatty acid from palm oil for lactating dairy cows is 6.52 (1.74) Mcal/kg DM.
the NEL for lactation of long-chain fatty acid salts of calcium from palm oil is 6.52 +/- 1.74 Mcal/kg DM.
the NEL of calcium long-chain fatty acids in palm oil for lactating cows is 6.52 (1.74) Mcal/kg DM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NEL of fat is 5.8 to 6.5 Mcal/kg DM and is not affected by dietary protein content.
NEL of calcium salt of long-chain fatty acid is 6.52 +/- 1.74 Mcal/kg DM.
the NEL of calcium soaps of long chain fatty acids (C16 and C18) is 6.52 +/- 1.74 Mcal/kg DM and that this value is independent of the dietary protein level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the efficiency of use of metabolizable or net energy from dietary fat is very high, which is consistent with the results from our previous work and with the results from the literature.
fat can be fed to lactating dairy cows without compromising milk production.
the energy in fat is utilized efficiently for milk production, but the efficiency is not 100%.
